title: Telemetry adapter negotiation and runtime shim for multi-version analytics
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Console backend receives telemetry from a mix of SDKs, CLI releases, and third-party integrations that each may be on different analytics schema versions. We currently rely on a brittle one-way migration path that forces older clients to either stop sending events or to be dropped at the ingestion layer. This creates blind spots in usage analytics and complicates rollouts for console and runtime changes.

Goal: Implement a lightweight runtime 'telemetry negotiation' shim in the console backend that: 1) negotiates event schema versions with upstream clients (SDK/CLI) via headers or handshake events, 2) applies deterministic enrichments/downgrades so events can be routed into existing pipelines without schema breakage, and 3) emits compatibility diagnostics into the telemetry observability stream to guide SDK/CLI rollouts. The solution must be observable, reversible, and safe for a canary rollout.

Constraints: Must not impact tokenized event throughput by more than 5% at p95; must preserve personally-identifiable data redaction rules; must be implementable without a full ingestion rewrite in this cycle. Rollout window is 6 weeks.

Non-goal: Full canonical migration of all downstream analytics consumers to the newest schema (that is a follow-up project).
acceptance_criteria: Console backend exposes a negotiation header (X-Telemetry-Schema: <version>, negotiation=1) and falls back to parsed event version when header absent.
Runtime shim can transform v1->v2 and v2->v1 for a defined subset of fields (user_id, route, duration_ms, error_code) with explicit field mapping table stored in configstore.
All transformed events include a compatibility_metadata tag in the event payload and a trace id for debugging.
End-to-end tests validating downgrade/upgrade transformations for SDK v1.4, SDK v1.7, and CLI v0.9 producing identical critical metrics (requests, failures, latency) within 2% of native ingestion.
Canary rollout plan implemented (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback if error rate or ingestion latency exceed thresholds.
A new dashboard tile in console-telemetry shows per-client-version event acceptance rate and transformation error counts.
Documentation updated: Confluence page describing negotiation protocol, SDK/CLI changes, and migration checklist.
Security review completed and any KMS/HSM interactions documented.
tasks: Design negotiation header semantics and default fallback behavior (ENG design doc).
Implement negotiation shim in console-backend ingestion path with pluggable adapters.
Create config-driven field mapping + transformation library (supports forward/backward mapping and defaulting).
Add compatibility_metadata to event envelope and propagate to Kafka topic 'telemetry.compatibility.v1'.
Add unit/integration tests covering transformation logic and redaction rules.
Instrument observability: histogram for transformation time, counter for transformation failures, and per-version acceptance gauge.
Implement canary release hooks in router to steer percentages and tie to feature flag.
Update SDK and CLI stubs with negotiation header and fallback behavior; publish test releases to internal beta users.
Write migration runbook and rollback steps; create Confluence checklist and a postmortem template for issues.
Schedule security review and submit PR for approval.
comments: 2025-02-20 Miguel Torres: Spike completed — prototype shim in sandbox can transform a small sample set of events (user_id, route). Perf cost ~2.1% p95 on sandbox machines. PR pending.

2025-02-21 Asha Kapoor: Decided to prefer header-based negotiation with event-version fallback to avoid forcing SDK upgrades immediately. Added requirement to surface compatibility metadata in telemetry topic.
2025-02-22 Miguel Torres: Created draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3124 — includes negotiation header parsing and naive mapping table. Needs tests and redaction checks.
2025-02-23 Rebecca Lin (Product): Reviewed and requested add'l acceptance criteria around analytics parity for billing metrics and SLAs. Marked customer_impact medium.
2025-02-24 SRE note: Add circuit breaker if transformation latency > 20ms for a sustained window to prevent tail latency propagation. Logged to ENG-12905 as follow-up.
2025-02-25 Miguel Torres: Updated PR with transformation metrics and started internal canary at 1% — initial dashboard shows 0 transformation failures over 3 hours.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal integration tests and unit tests (complete).
Phase 1: internal canary to 1% traffic for 48h; validate transformation_latency_ms and failure_count against thresholds.
Phase 2: increase to 10% for 72h; run synthetic billing and usage queries to verify parity.
Phase 3: 50% for 7 days; collect stakeholder signoff (analytics, billing, SRE).
Phase 4: full rollout to 100% and monitor for 14 days before marking Done.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Transformation logic could accidentally drop newly-added fields leading to analytics regressions. Mitigation: add strict schema tests and 'opt-in' toggles per-field in the mapping config.
Risk: Increased tail latency could violate console SLOs. Mitigation: circuit breaker that bypasses transformation and tags events as 'untransformed' when thresholds hit.

Risk: SDK/CLI adoption slowness leaves legacy versions active. Mitigation: emit version-specific diagnostic reports and coordinate with SDK owners to push updates; plan rollback path if incompatibility persists.
